common_name: Escapade White Plumbago (Compact Seed-Grown White Cape Plumbago)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once nights stay reliably above 50°F; this F1 seed strain flowers the first year and suits mixed containers and hanging baskets as well as garden beds.

directions: Unlike most Cape plumbago selections, which are propagated as rooted cuttings, Escapade White is a first-generation (F1) seed strain that flowers reliably in its first season, producing pure white clusters on a bushy, horizontally spreading plant that runs shorter but wider than its blue-flowered Escapade counterpart. It branches well without pinching and shrugs off summer heat and swings between wet and dry soil better than many older vegetatively propagated cultivars. Because it is an F1 hybrid, any self-sown seedlings that appear will likely revert toward the species and should not be relied on to come true. Give it full sun and well-drained soil, and expect a long bloom run from late spring into fall in zone 9-11 gardens or as a warm-season annual further north.

planting.note: Plant container-grown Monite in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; its dense, compact habit and patented parentage make it best sourced as a rooted nursery liner rather than grown from seed.

directions: Monite arose as a naturally occurring whole-plant mutation discovered in a planting of the deep-blue 'Monott' (Royal Cape) cultivar and is marketed under the trade name White Cape, distinct from the older, looser-habited white cultivar 'Alba'. It carries larger, wider petals and blooms more densely than typical white plumbagos, on a noticeably tighter, more compact frame than the straight species. Site it in full sun with well-drained, moderately fertile soil, and expect nearly continuous white bloom from spring through frost in zone 9 conditions. Where winters bring hard freezes, plants die back to the root but recover quickly and resume flowering by late spring; cut back cold-damaged wood in late winter to keep the habit dense.

common_name: Dark Blue Plumbago (Large-Growing Medium-Blue Cape Plumbago)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; give it plenty of room or a fence/trellis to climb, since it grows larger than most named Cape plumbago selections.

directions: Dark Blue is a widely distributed wholesale nursery selection valued for producing more richly saturated, medium-blue flower clusters than the pale sky-blue typical of seedling-grown Cape plumbago, on a notably larger, more vigorous plant. Left untrained it mounds and sprawls into a wide, arching mass, but it also takes readily to being tied up and trained as an informal flowering vine against a fence, wall, or trellis. Give it full sun and well-drained soil; established plants tolerate heat, drought, and the sandy, salt-affected soils common near the Gulf Coast. In zone 8 winters, hard freezes typically kill the plant back to the ground, but it resprouts vigorously from the roots and returns to bloom by early summer; prune out dead wood in late winter before new growth begins.
